sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides visual cues that are mostly timed to the narrated references, while Lesson 1 has no beat/timing cue data at all, making its visual-narration synchronization unverified and effectively unsupported for this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 is conceptually correct and pedagogically builds the solution through decomposition, vertical flight time, and horizontal range, whereas Lesson 1 gives the correct numerical range but largely skips the equations/derivation and relies on a Desmos endpoint reading with a distracting erroneous ending.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a cleaner, more visually consistent dark layout with centered readable title content, while Lesson 1 is cluttered by large UI/chat elements, has off-center content with excessive empty space, and its mid-lesson Desmos/caption layout feels busy and overlapping.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents preferred Lesson 2, with consistently high confidence. Lesson 2 was judged superior in visual accuracy due to its correct projectile diagram and clearer graphing, in interactivity because it includes a functional fill-in checkpoint, in narration quality for clearer pacing and fewer defects, in synchronization because its visuals align with narration, in conceptual accuracy because it builds the solution through decomposition and equations, and in polish because it has a cleaner, more readable layout. Lesson 1 had multiple issues including incomplete or unsupported visuals, no functional checkpoint evidence, awkward narration with an unrelated fragment, missing timing data, limited derivation, and cluttered layout. The verdict is therefore clearly Lesson 2.
